title: You think God only uses clean people?
paragraphs: You think God only uses clean people?

Because Hebrews 11 is not a gallery of perfection…
It’s a graveyard of shame that God turned into glory.
And if you read too fast—you’ll miss it.

We celebrate them like giants.
But heaven remembers them as people who almost didn’t make it.

Abel worshiped right… and got killed for it. (Genesis 4:4–8)
Noah obeyed when the sky was still empty. (Genesis 6:22)
Abraham lied about his wife—twice. (Genesis 12:13; 20:2)
Sarah laughed at God’s promise. (Genesis 18:12)
Moses murdered a man and ran. (Exodus 2:12)
Rahab sold her body… before she surrendered her life. (Joshua 2:1)
These are not Sunday school heroes.
And maybe that’s what unsettles you.

Because deep down…
you know your story fits closer to theirs than you’d like to admit.

The hidden compromise.
The quiet addiction.
The pride no one sees.
The past you rehearse in your mind at night.
You’re not struggling to be perfect.
You’re struggling to believe you’re still usable.

Hebrews 11 never hides their brokenness.
It just refuses to let brokenness be the final word.
“By faith… Abel… Noah… Abraham… Sarah… Moses… Rahab…” (Hebrews 11)
Because faith is not pretending you’re strong.
Faith is clinging to God when you know you’re not.

Because if you misunderstand this…
you will turn grace into an excuse instead of a rescue.
“Now faith is confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.” (Hebrews 11:1)

It is a fierce, trembling, stubborn trust in God’s Word
even when your life doesn’t match it yet.

Some scholars interpret Hebrews 11 as a courtroom of testimony—
each life standing as evidence that trusting God is worth it.
Even when it doesn’t end the way you hoped.

Some of them conquered kingdoms.
Others were tortured.

Some shut the mouths of lions.
Others were sawn in two.
“These were all commended for their faith, yet none of them received what had been promised…” (Hebrews 11:39)

They had faith…
but didn’t receive the full promise?
Because their story was pointing forward.
And this is where everything turns.
You are not saved by having faith like Abraham.
You are saved by placing your faith in Jesus Christ.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
But God didn’t leave it there.
Jesus stepped into the story they were waiting for.

He lived the life we couldn’t live…
and died the death we deserved.
“God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Your failure met His finished work.
“If you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.” (Romans 10:9)
So what does that mean for you?
It means your past is not your identity.
It means your failure is not your ending.
It means your secret sin is not stronger than God’s grace.
But it also means something uncomfortable.

You cannot hold on to sin
and hold on to Jesus at the same time.
Turning from the lie that you can fix yourself.
Because the same God who wrote Hebrews 11…
And your name is not disqualified.

“Jesus, I need You.
Forgive me.
Change me.
I trust You.”
